ahead: CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md's Energy(N) is an exact identity (not just a domination), true for every real vector by pure linear algebra -- confirmed independently here by running the identical construction on a Davenport-Heilbronn sequence (zeta/epstein.py), which also violates RH, and getting the same exact equality. Any future work on Section 8 should not treat CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md's domination as progress toward bounding E_corr(N) or toward RH; it is a content-free repackaging. The open problem is unchanged: find a domination that uses something specific to Lambda/primes/the singular series, not just that x is a real vector.

work.what: Section 8 needs a genuinely arithmetic multiscale (or other) upper bound Energy(N) >= E_corr(N) := 2 sum_{h=1}^N |r_N(h) - C_N(h)|^2, where r_N(h) = psi_2(N,h) - (N-h)*S(h) is the CHHL prime-pair correlation residual (psi_2(N,h) = sum_{n=1}^{N-h} Lambda(n) Lambda(n+h), Lambda the von Mangoldt function including proper prime powers, S the singular series), and C_N(h) is the exceptional-zero correction of SIEGEL_UNIFORMITY.md equation (5) (C_N = 0 if no exceptional zero exists at that N). The known candidate in CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md's Section 2 (a dyadic block-average / Haar telescoping of the residual vector padded to a power-of-2 length) fails to be useful: it is proved (and independently reverified) to be an EXACT identity Energy(N) = E_corr(N) for every N, using only that the vector is real -- it uses no property of Lambda, S, or C_N at all. Proof: it survives being applied verbatim to a Davenport-Heilbronn sequence (real coefficients, a genuine functional equation, a zero off the critical line) with the identical result to 16 digits (see hunts/prime_pair_error/CHALLENGE.md and results_s8_challenge.json, attack 2). A useful next candidate must break that: it needs to actually use positivity, size, or distributional properties of Lambda/S/C_N (e.g. a second-moment / large-sieve type bound, an explicit-formula input, or a sieve bound) so that the SAME construction applied to the Davenport-Heilbronn (or Epstein) counterexample battery of zeta/epstein.py does NOT give a matching bound, since that counterexample is known to violate RH. Constraints inherited from Section 8 (retain the mean/central mode, retain cross terms between scales rather than dropping them, handle changing exceptional data q/chi/beta with N, keep the sharp endpoint N-h with no smoothing, no primes-only replacement of Lambda) still apply and should be checked against whatever new construction is tried, the same way CANDIDATE_ENERGY.md's Section 8 did for its own attempt.
